newsitem.title: POLAND: SAB PARTNERSHIP TO INVEST $200 MLN IN POLAND.
newsitem.headline: SAB PARTNERSHIP TO INVEST $200 MLN IN POLAND.

text.p: Poland's largest brewery group, in which South African Breweries Ltd (SAB) has a strategic stake, plans to double its investment in Poland to about $400 million in five years, Meyer Kahen, SAB group chairman, said on Tuesday.
"The partnership has invested close to $200 million in our current production and our planning spread over the next five years...adds up to another $200 million," Kahn said.
He told a news conference the investment was needed largely to strengthen distribution and boost production at two large breweries, Tychy and Lech, in which SAB had stakes.
SAB and a local company called Euro Agro Centrum SA jointly hold a 75 percent stake in the Tychy brewery in southern Poland. It also indirectly holds 27.5 percent in Lech, in western Poland.

Kahn said SAB had completed its recent $160 million investment programme in Hungary, where its two brewers have a 40 percent market share, and could double its investment in Romania of up to $60 million over the next few years.
SAB has stakes in three Romanian brewers.

Kahn said he saw Lech and Tychy, both of which SAB entered last year, increasing their total annual sales to about six million hectolitres annually from the current three million by about the year 2002.

He said SAB's Hungarian firms could increase annual sales over the next few years toward four million hectolitres annually from the current three million and its Romanian firms might need three to five years to lift sales to five million hectolitres annually from the current 1.5 million.
Malcolm Wyman, SAB's finance and development director, added the firm had no immediate plans to buy another brewer in the region but was mulling further acquisitions, possibly in CIS countries.
Kahn was particularly bullish on the Polish market, where currently about 17 million hectolitres of beer are produced each year.
"The Polish beer market is most certain going to grow at a minimum to 25 million hectolitres by about the year 2002," he told Reuters.
